message.content:
The cost of renting an apartment in New York City varies widely depending on several key factors:

| Factor | Typical Impact |
|--------|----------------|
| **Neighborhood** | Manhattan (especially mid‑town, Upper East Side, Tribeca) tends to be the most expensive; Brooklyn and Queens offer more affordable options. |
| **Apartment Size & Type** | Studio apartments start around $1,500–$2,000/month in Manhattan; one‑bedroom units often range from $2,200–$3,800. Two‑bedrooms can exceed $4,000 in prime locations. |
| **Building Amenities** | Buildings with doormen, gyms, concierge services, or rooftop decks usually charge a premium—often adding $300–$700/month to rent. |
| **Lease Length & Timing** | Short‑term leases or last‑minute moves may incur higher rates. Signing during peak move‑in seasons (summer/fall) can also affect pricing. |
| **Market Conditions** | Rental prices fluctuate with supply/demand cycles, economic shifts, and regulatory changes (e.g., rent‑control laws). |

### Rough Price Ranges (as of early 2026)

| Neighborhood | Average Monthly Rent (Studio) | Average Monthly Rent (1‑Bed) | Average Monthly Rent (2‑Bed) |
|--------------|-------------------------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Manhattan – Midtown | $1,600 | $2,400 | $3,800 |
| Manhattan – Upper West Side | $1,700 | $2,500 | $4,100 |
| Brooklyn – Williamsburg | $1,900 | $2,800 | $4,200 |
| Brooklyn – Bushwick | $1,400 | $2,200 | $3,200 |
| Queens – Long Island City | $1,800 | $2,600 | $3,900 |
| Bronx – Fordham | $1,200 | $1,800 | $2,500 |

> **Note:** These figures are averages; actual rents can differ based on exact address, unit condition, lease terms, and additional fees (security deposit, broker’s commission, utilities).

If you’re looking for a specific area or have a budget in mind, let me know and I can narrow down the options further!
